2.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() takes round(inputs[OFFSET_CV_INPUT].getVoltage() * 7.f * 0.1f) as a whole-cell offset, adds it to the knob and clamps the total to 0..7

3.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() clamps inputs[RULE_CV_INPUT].getVoltage() * 0.1f to -1..1; wolfEngine.cpp setRuleCv rounds that to a whole rule over 256, lifeEngine.cpp over 30

4.why: src/Wolfram.cpp setEngine() rounds inputs[ENGINE_CV_INPUT].getVoltage() * 0.1f times one and clamps it to 0..1, so it picks one of the two algorithms

5.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() calls trigTrigger.process(stepVoltage, 0.1f, 2.f) on inputs[TRIG_INPUT].getVoltage() with no channel; in audioRateMode the same voltage is tested for zero crossings instead

comment: Read from the maker's source and the Wolfram manual PDF in the repository, at commit 2dca0ad, the head of main. Six commits carry the installed 2.1.1: 3dea33b, f35a698, ff40356, the merge 5d039d0, 54611e3 and 2dca0ad. The installed build settles which side of f35a698 shipped: that commit replaced the two hidden slew Trimpots with a new TrimpotGreen class and added res/components/TrimpotGreen.svg, and the installed build uses TrimpotGreen, with both SVG files in the installed res folder. Everything after f35a698 is comment and whitespace in Wolfram.cpp plus a manual rename, so the installed build behaves as 2dca0ad does. Panel names were read from a render of res/panels/wolfram.svg and are shorter than the maker's configured names: SEL for 'Rule', LEN for 'Length', PROB for 'Probability', ALGO for 'Algorithm CV', XOUT, XPULSE, YOUT and YPULSE for 'X', 'X Pulse', 'Y' and 'Y Pulse'. The three trimpots carry no panel lettering at all; the word OFFSET on the panel is 7mm below the offset CV jack at y 99.852 and labels that jack, not the trimpot at y 80.597. Index order is not panel order for the inputs: the census order is Reset, Probability CV, Offset CV, Rule CV, Algorithm CV, Trigger, Inject, while the bottom row runs TRIG, INJECT, PROB, RULE, ALGO left to right and the offset jack is in the row above, so inputs 5 and 6 are the leftmost two jacks of the bottom row. Outputs are not in panel order either: index 3 (Y Pulse) is left of index 2 (Y). X Gain and X Slew share one position, as do Y Gain and Y Slew; only one of each pair is visible at a time, switched by the menu's FX page, so all four are reachable and all four are tagged. The manual names the menu's third page 'Slew' where the display prints ' FX ' and offers GAIN and SLEW; the code is followed here. The manual says Life's Y PULSE is high when the population dies or becomes static; lifeEngine.cpp renderOutput also fires it when the grid alternates between two states, which the lines include. The X and Y lamps are set from a value already clamped to 0..1 and then multiplied by 0.1, so they never rise above a tenth brightness; no line depends on them.
